title: Пять килограммов с Мадагаскара  (Five Kilograms from Madagascar)

segments.t: At the loading dock, supplier Timur hands Senya a huge crate of five kilograms of Madagascar cockroaches instead of five individual bugs, and mentions spotting Eleonora Andreevna nearby. Listen to the conversation.
Смотри, свежайший товар привёз.
Они ещё с утра завтракали.
Зачем ты так много привёз?
Вы сами просили пять килограмм.
Мы просили только пять штук.
Я по одному их не продаю.
Не купишь ты — купят другие.
Их купят в китайском ресторане.
Ладно, давай их сюда.
Доброе утро, Тимур.
Я Элеонору Андреевну встретил на улице.
Она нашла нас на новом месте.
Ты меня всегда отлично кормил, шеф.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
Смотри, свежайший товар привёз.
'Look, I brought the freshest goods.' The meaning hinges on 'watch' working together with 'brought' in spoken Russian.
Они ещё с утра завтракали.
'They were still having breakfast this morning.' Notice how Russian expresses 'they' and 'had breakfast' with crisp inflection rather than helper words. Senya answers right away.
Зачем ты так много привёз?
'Why did you bring so much?' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'why' and finishing on 'brought'.
Вы сами просили пять килограмм.
'You yourselves asked for five kilograms.' In Russian, the idea of 'you' flows naturally into 'kilograms' without extra filler words.
Мы просили только пять штук.
'We asked for only five individual ones.' The plural past ending '-li' on the verb for 'to ask' covers a group or the polite 'you'. Timur answers right away.
Я по одному их не продаю.
'I do not sell them one by one.' Timur brings out the contrast between 'I' and 'according to' in a few short words.
Не купишь ты — купят другие.
'If you do not buy them, others will.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'not' and finishing on 'other'.
Их купят в китайском ресторане.
'They will buy them at the Chinese restaurant.' The grammar packs 'their' and 'restaurant' into a tight, idiomatic kitchen exchange. Senya answers right away.
Ладно, давай их сюда.
'Fine, hand them over here.' The meaning hinges on 'all right' working together with 'here' in spoken Russian.
Доброе утро, Тимур.
'Good morning, Timur.' In Russian, the idea of 'good' flows naturally into 'Timur' without extra filler words.
Я Элеонору Андреевну встретил на улице.
'I met Eleonora Andreevna on the street.' Notice how Russian expresses 'I' and 'street' with crisp inflection rather than helper words.
Она нашла нас на новом месте.
'She found us at the new place.' Here the Russian phrasing highlights 'she' before landing on 'place'.
Ты меня всегда отлично кормил, шеф.
'You always fed me great, Chef.' Spoken Russian keeps this brisk, leaning on 'you' and finishing on 'proper name'. Alright, let's hear the entire conversation one more time from start to finish.
